headline: Protest group mocks Meta's Kylie Jenner smart glasses with 'We're Always Watching' bus ads in London
summary: Activist group Everyone Hates Elon installed lenticular spoof ads at London bus stops, transforming Kylie Jenner's Meta glasses campaign into a 'We're Always Watching' privacy warning.
details: The activist group Everyone Hates Elon (EHE) installed lenticular spoof ads at a London bus stop near Meta's headquarters, targeting Meta's smart glasses campaign featuring Kylie Jenner. The ads visually transform from Jenner wearing the glasses to an X-ray image with the tagline 'We're always watching,' highlighting privacy concerns.

The ad's transformation element references the politically charged sci-fi film They Live, where special sunglasses expose hidden messages and control. EHE aims to confront Meta's 'encroaching surveillance mechanisms' through this public intervention.

Meta's latest Ray-Ban smart glasses allow up to three minutes of consecutive recording, raising concerns about unknowingly being recorded in public. The product has faced extensive online criticism, particularly due to its popularity among 'Manosphere' content creators using them to record women without consent.

An EHE spokesperson stated, 'Meta has spent years tracking us online. Now it wants to track us in the real world too,' calling the use for recording women without consent 'abuse.' Harvard researchers in 2024 demonstrated facial recognition on footage from these glasses, locating personal information from public databases.

The rapid evolution of smart glasses and AI technology processing biometric data has outpaced privacy law and ethical considerations. EHE questions why billionaires fund such devices instead of addressing critical societal issues.

headline_marked: [[Voicebox, an open-source voice-to-text tool]], uses Cloudflare AI with a free tier
headline: Voicebox, an open-source voice-to-text tool, uses Cloudflare AI with a free tier
summary: This tool captures speech via a hotkey, transcribes it with Whisper, and formats the output using an LLM, then auto-pastes it into your active application. It offers a free tier and leverages Cloudflare AI for processing.
details: Voicebox is an open-source voice-to-text tool designed for instant transcription and formatting. Users press a hotkey to speak, release it, and the formatted text automatically appears in their clipboard and is pasted into the active application.
The tool leverages OpenAI's Whisper for transcription and an LLM for intelligent formatting. It also utilizes Cloudflare AI for its processing capabilities, offering a free tier for users.

Configuration can be managed through a settings window that opens on launch or via a manual config file located at ~/.config/voicebox/voicebox.toml. Auto-paste functionality on macOS requires Accessibility access, which the system prompts for on first use.

During recording, a compact overlay appears, displaying a recording indicator, voice level meter, and status updates. The system sends a configure message with audio parameters and context about the focused application element (e.g., app name, input field type) to the LLM for tailored output.
